resources.string: A qualitative cross-section of one human scalp follicle in a typical cycle. Shapes and motion are simplified and not to scale. Chapters do not show real durations; follicles cycle independently, and shedding and renewed growth need not coincide. This is anatomy education, not health advice.
In the bulb at the base of the growing follicle, matrix cells divide. Some of their descendants form the hair shaft.
Cells that form the shaft harden as they mature. New shaft material added at the base moves the existing shaft outward; growth does not occur at the tip.
Shaft growth stops, the lower follicle shortens, and the base of the old shaft rounds into a club root. The upper follicle stays in place.
The shortened follicle can hold the old club hair without lengthening it. The moving ring only highlights the retained root.
During shedding (exogen), the club hair releases. A new shaft forms at the base as the same follicle re-enters anagen. These events are shown together, but one does not have to trigger the other.
Soma et al. (1998): Cell death during human hair follicle regression
Van Neste et al. (2007): Exogen hair characterization in human scalp
